hero.headline: Trump to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
hero.body:
President Trump announced at a White House dinner that he plans to nominate Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general, according to a video of the event posted on social media by a White House aide.

Blanche has previously represented Trump in multiple legal matters and currently serves as deputy attorney general. If confirmed by the Senate, he would lead the Department of Justice and serve as the chief law enforcement officer of the federal government. The attorney general position ranks among the most powerful roles in the executive branch, with authority over federal prosecutions, civil rights enforcement, and antitrust matters. The Justice Department also oversees agencies including the FBI and the Bureau of Prisons.

The nomination requires Senate confirmation. The Senate Judiciary Committee will hold hearings to review Blanche's qualifications and record before the full Senate votes on his confirmation. Trump has not yet submitted the formal nomination paperwork to the Senate, but once submitted, the confirmation process will begin with committee review.

Blanche's potential confirmation comes amid controversy over his handling of documents related to Jeffrey Epstein. A lawsuit filed Monday by Katie Phang, an investigative journalist and legal analyst, alleges that Blanche engaged in a "brazen, shocking, and ongoing violation" of a law requiring the Department of Justice to release all documents related to the late sex offender.

Congress passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act in November with a December 19, 2025 deadline for releasing all documents. Phang's lawsuit claims that Blanche has missed statutory deadlines for document production, made improper or excessive redactions, failed to explain redactions as required by law, and withheld or retracted key documents after release. Blanche has argued that redactions were necessary to prevent the inadvertent identification of Epstein's victims, many of whom are minors, though he has acknowledged that "mistakes are inevitable."

Democratic lawmakers have criticized the process. Jamie Raskin, the Democratic ranking member of the House judiciary committee, told reporters in February that there were "tons of completely unnecessary redactions, in addition to the failure to redact the names of victims."

Phang wants the court to declare the Department of Justice in violation of the law and order the release of all required documents without unlawful redactions. The lawsuit also seeks the appointment of an independent special master from outside the department to oversee the agency's compliance with the transparency law.

The Justice Department's office of the inspector general announced last week that it was launching its own audit into the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act, with a preliminary objective of evaluating the agency's processes for identifying, redacting, and releasing records.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah withdrawal
cards.teaser: Israel and Lebanon reached an agreement for a full ceasefire, conditioned on Hezbollah halting attacks and withdrawing operatives from southern Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a full ceasefire to end hostilities, according to a joint statement from the US State Department. The agreement requires Hezbollah to completely cease fire and withdraw all its fighters from the area south of the Litani River in south Lebanon.

The US emphasized that both countries reject "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage." The ceasefire represents a significant development in the Trump administration's broader diplomatic efforts in the Middle East, removing one of the largest barriers to reaching a wider agreement with Iran.

cards.headline: Hungary lifts veto on Ukraine's EU membership bid
cards.teaser: Hungary announced a deal with Ukraine on minority rights, clearing the path for Kyiv to begin EU entry talks.
cards.body:
Hungary has lifted its 17-month veto on Ukraine's EU membership bid following an agreement on minority rights. The deal addresses Hungarian concerns about the treatment of ethnic Hungarians in Ukraine and clears the path for Kyiv to begin EU accession talks.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar signaled a new approach to Ukraine relations, indicating Hungary's willingness to host peace talks and meet with Ukrainian President Zelenskiy. The breakthrough marks a significant shift from Hungary's previous stance under Viktor Orbán's leadership.

cards.headline: US House votes to limit Trump's war powers on Iran
cards.teaser: Four Republicans joined Democrats to pass a measure constraining presidential military authority.
cards.body:
The US House of Representatives voted 215-208 to pass a war powers resolution limiting presidential authority over military operations against Iran. The measure required Trump to seek congressional approval before conducting military action or withdraw US forces from the region. Four Republicans crossed party lines to support the measure alongside Democrats: Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Warren Davidson of Ohio, and Tom Barrett of Michigan.

The passage marked a significant rebuke of executive power after three previous failed attempts to advance similar legislation. The vote demonstrated bipartisan concern over unchecked presidential authority in decisions about military engagement with Iran.

cards.headline: Trump removes job protections from 8,000 federal workers
cards.teaser: President Trump signed an executive order stripping civil service protections from thousands of senior federal employees.
cards.body:
President Trump signed an executive order removing job protections from approximately 8,000 senior federal workers earning up to nearly $200,000 annually. These employees, deemed to be "influencing" government policy, are now classified in a way that allows them to be fired without the standard civil service protections.

The change gives the administration greater flexibility to dismiss these high-ranking personnel without the lengthy removal processes typically required for protected federal employees. The order is part of a broader effort to overhaul the federal workforce.

cards.headline: SpaceX sets $135 share price for record-breaking public offering
cards.body:
SpaceX announced a target share price of $135 per share as it prepares for what would be the largest stock market debut in history. The space exploration company founded by Elon Musk set the price earlier than market analysts expected, according to multiple reports.

The offering will consist of 555.6 million shares at the $135 price point, establishing a total valuation of $1.77 trillion for the company. This valuation would make SpaceX worth more than any other company has been valued at during an initial public offering. The shares are expected to begin trading as early as Thursday, though the exact timing was not confirmed in available reports.

The planned IPO comes amid questions from some market observers about whether the company's valuation is justified. Some analysts have expressed concern that SpaceX may be significantly overvalued at the proposed price, though the company has maintained its operations in commercial spaceflight, satellite internet through its Starlink division, and contracts with government agencies including NASA.

SpaceX has been operating as a privately held company since its founding, with funding coming from private investment rounds. The decision to go public represents a significant shift in the company's capital structure and will subject it to the disclosure requirements and quarterly reporting obligations that come with being a publicly traded corporation.

The timing of the offering puts SpaceX on track to raise substantial capital that the company can use for its ongoing operations and future expansion plans. The successful completion of the IPO would give public market investors their first opportunity to buy shares in the space exploration company, which has grown from a startup into one of the most prominent players in the commercial space industry.

cards.headline: Iranian attack on Kuwait airport kills one, injures dozens
cards.body:
An Iranian attack on Kuwait's airport killed one person and injured dozens, Kuwaiti officials said. The attack involved Iranian drones striking the airport facility. Kuwait condemned what it described as brutal and ongoing Iranian attacks.

The incident occurred as a renewed cease-fire between Israel and Lebanon was announced. The timing raised questions about whether the cease-fire, which depends on cooperation from Iran-backed Hezbollah, could help reduce broader regional tensions. The United States brokered the Lebanon agreement and is also engaged in separate negotiations with Iran.

Kuwait, a US ally in the Persian Gulf, issued a statement condemning the Iranian strikes. The attack on civilian airport infrastructure represents a significant escalation in Iranian military activity in the region. Kuwait has historically maintained a more neutral stance in regional conflicts compared to some of its Gulf neighbors.

The attack comes as Iran faces multiple diplomatic and military pressures. Iranian officials are working to secure visas for their national soccer team to attend the World Cup, which begins next week in the United States. The US House of Representatives voted to limit presidential war powers related to Iran, with four Republicans joining Democrats in the 215-208 vote.

The strike on Kuwait adds another layer of complexity to regional security dynamics. Iran backs Hezbollah in Lebanon and has been involved in various proxy conflicts across the Middle East. The attack on a US ally's airport infrastructure could complicate ongoing diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran, even as both countries have interests in stabilizing parts of the region.

cards.teaser: The US-brokered agreement calls for a complete cessation of fire from Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.
cards.body:

The agreement is contingent on a complete cessation of fire from Hezbollah, the Iran-aligned militia operating in southern Lebanon, and requires the evacuation of all its fighters from the area south of the Litani River.

cards.teaser: Hungary announced a deal with Ukraine on minority rights, clearing the path for Kyiv to begin EU entry talks.
cards.body:
Hungary has lifted its 17-month veto on Ukraine's EU membership bid following an agreement on minority rights. The deal addresses Hungarian concerns about the treatment of ethnic Hungarians in Ukraine and clears the path for Kyiv to begin EU accession talks.

cards.headline: Germany fails to win UN Security Council seat
cards.teaser: Germany blamed Russia for its defeat in the UN Security Council election, calling it a bitter diplomatic setback.
cards.body:
Germany's bid for a seat on the UN Security Council has failed. According to German officials, Russia actively worked against Germany's candidacy due to Berlin's support for Ukraine. Five countries were elected to the council instead, including Kyrgyzstan, which secured a seat for the first time.

The loss marks a significant diplomatic setback for Chancellor Merz. Germany had pursued the Security Council position as part of its broader strategy to expand its role in international security matters.

cards.headline: Protests enter third day over Trump-linked resort in Albania
cards.teaser: Demonstrations continue over a controversial luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner on Sazan Island.
cards.body:
Thousands of Albanians demonstrated for a third consecutive day in Tirana against a luxury resort project backed by Jared Kushner. Protesters, some carrying inflatable flamingos to symbolize environmental concerns, are calling for the project to be blocked.

The government-approved development on Sazan Island has drawn opposition from conservation groups and critics who question its environmental impact and transparency. Prime Minister offered to discuss solutions, but protesters rejected the offer. The government says the project will bring jobs and investment to the nation.

cards.headline: China bans four New Zealand lawmakers over Taiwan visit
cards.teaser: The MPs were informed of a one-year ban after returning from Taiwan last month.
cards.body:
China has imposed a one-year ban on four New Zealand members of parliament following their visit to Taiwan. The lawmakers learned of the restriction upon returning home last month.

Beijing views Taiwan as part of its territory and regularly responds to foreign officials' engagement with Taiwanese authorities through diplomatic measures. New Zealand does not formally recognize Taiwan as independent but maintains unofficial relations with the island.

hero.headline: Trump removes job protections from 8,000 federal workers
hero.teaser: President Trump signed an executive order stripping civil service protections from thousands of senior federal employees.
hero.body:
President Trump signed an executive order removing job protections from approximately 8,000 senior federal workers earning up to nearly $200,000 annually. These employees, deemed to be "influencing" government policy, are now classified in a way that allows them to be fired without the standard civil service protections.

The change gives the administration greater flexibility to dismiss these high-ranking personnel without the lengthy removal processes typically required for protected federal employees. The order is part of a broader effort to overhaul the federal workforce.

cards.headline: Trump to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.teaser: President Trump announced plans to formally nominate Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general.
cards.body:
President Trump announced at a White House dinner that he plans to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general. The announcement was captured in a video posted on social media by a White House aide.

Blanche's nomination would formalize his role within the Department of Justice. Republican senators are watching for his signals on DOJ funding decisions.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm found in Texas cattle
cards.teaser: Officials confirmed the first case of flesh-eating screwworm in the United States, detected in a Texas calf.
cards.body:
Federal and state officials confirmed the presence of flesh-eating screwworm in a Texas calf, marking the first case of the parasite in United States cattle. The pest crossed the border from Mexico, according to authorities.

Screwworm is a parasite that feeds on living tissue in animals and can be fatal if untreated. The U.S. Department of Agriculture has been tracking the situation. The discovery raises concerns about potential spread to other livestock in the region.

cards.headline: Ohio State settles for $100 million with sexual abuse survivors
cards.teaser: Ohio State University reached a $100 million settlement with hundreds of people who say they were abused by a school doctor.
cards.body:
Ohio State University agreed to a $100 million settlement with hundreds of survivors who were sexually abused by former university doctor Richard Strauss. The settlement resolves a lawsuit that had been proceeding against the institution over the abuse claims.

Strauss, who worked at the university for decades, was accused of sexually abusing students and athletes during his employment. The settlement concludes litigation from the remaining survivors and brings the case to a close.

cards.headline: New York Democrats advance redistricting amendment
cards.teaser: New York state lawmakers gave preliminary approval to a redistricting amendment that could reshape congressional maps.
cards.body:
New York Democrats in the state legislature gave preliminary approval to an amendment that would allow mid-decade redistricting. The measure is designed to help the party retain House seats in the 2028 elections.

The proposed legislation would enable Democrats to redraw district lines before the next census cycle, part of what they describe as an aggressive redistricting strategy aimed at gaining additional congressional seats in the state.

cards.headline: Trump family-linked resort project faces protests in Albania
cards.teaser: A coastal development project in Albania connected to Jared Kushner is drawing opposition from environmental groups.
cards.body:
A coastal resort development backed by Jared Kushner is drawing fierce opposition in Albania, despite government support for the project. The Albanian prime minister argues it will bring jobs and investment to transform the nation's economy.

Environmental groups and conservation advocates have mobilized significant public resistance. Thousands of protesters took to the streets of Tirana for multiple consecutive days, with demonstrators even carrying inflatable flamingos to highlight environmental concerns. Critics claim work has begun in a protected coastal area, and they have rejected the prime minister's offer to discuss solutions, calling instead for the project to be blocked entirely.

cards.headline: Reality TV couple Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury have second child
cards.teaser: Reality television personalities Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury announced the birth of their second child.
cards.body:
Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury have welcomed their second child together. The Love Island stars announced the arrival on Instagram, sharing a photo featuring the couple with their daughter Bambi and their newborn.

The announcement marks the expansion of their family following the birth of their first daughter.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating parasite detected in U.S. cattle for first time since 1960s
cards.teaser: Agriculture officials confirmed the New World screwworm in a calf in South Texas.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed the presence of New World screwworm in a calf in South Texas, marking the first domestic case since the 1960s. The parasitic pest threatens livestock across the region.

This discovery represents a significant concern for agricultural authorities who have not dealt with the parasite domestically for over six decades.

cards.headline: Stock markets decline as Middle East tensions escalate
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell more than 600 points as conflict in the region intensified.
cards.body:
U.S. stock markets closed lower on Wednesday with the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropping 620 points. The decline reflected escalating tensions in the Middle East, with ongoing clashes between U.S. and Iranian forces unsettling investors.

Oil prices climbed to their highest level in more than a week as the Strait of Hormuz remained closed. The combination of declining oil inventories and the continued blockade of the strategic waterway intensified pressure on energy markets and contributed to broader stock market volatility.

cards.headline: Quantinuum prices quantum computing IPO at $60 per share
cards.teaser: The quantum computing company raised $1.68 billion and is scheduled to begin trading Thursday.
cards.body:
Quantinuum, the quantum computing company spun out of Honeywell, priced its initial public offering at $60 per share. The offering raised $1.68 billion, exceeding the company's initial plans.

The IPO values Quantinuum at more than $14 billion. Trading began Thursday, positioning Quantinuum as one of the first pure-play quantum computing companies available to public investors as interest in the technology accelerates.

cards.headline: Pace Gallery cuts 50 artists and 50 staff positions
cards.teaser: The established art gallery is contracting operations in response to challenging market conditions.
cards.body:
Pace Gallery is removing 50 artists from its roster and laying off 50 staff members as it navigates a challenging art market. The dual reduction signals the pressures facing established galleries in the contemporary art sector.

The cuts reflect broader economic headwinds affecting art dealers. By contracting both its artist representation and workforce, Pace is adjusting its operations to match current market conditions.

cards.headline: Broadcom shares fall despite increased revenue from AI chip demand
cards.teaser: The semiconductor company posted record quarterly earnings but saw its stock decline.
cards.body:
Broadcom shares dropped following the company's quarterly earnings report despite posting record revenue driven by demand for artificial intelligence chips. The company reported a jump in overall revenue but disappointed investors with weak software sales.

Broadcom also left its AI chip forecast for the year unchanged, which failed to meet investor expectations for stronger growth projections. The semiconductor company's quarterly results showed strength in its chip business but continued challenges in its software division contributed to the negative market reaction.

cards.headline: Colorado governor vetoes credit card swipe fee limits and firefighter cancer bill
cards.teaser: Governor Jared Polis rejected legislation that would have capped merchant fees and expanded benefits.
cards.body:
Colorado Governor Jared Polis vetoed legislation that would have limited credit card swipe fees charged to merchants. The governor also rejected a separate bill that would have provided additional support for firefighters who develop cancer.

The vetoes set a personal record for Polis in the number of bills rejected. Business groups representing electronic payment processors praised the veto of the swipe fee legislation, while small business advocates expressed disappointment that the measure did not become law.

hero.headline: NASA ends MAVEN Mars mission after spacecraft loses control
hero.body:
NASA has ended its MAVEN Mars mission after losing contact with the spacecraft, which entered an unrecoverable state while orbiting the red planet. The Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution mission, launched in 2013, stopped communicating with ground stations over the weekend after more than a decade of successful operations.

The spacecraft was functioning normally before passing behind Mars. When it reappeared from behind the planet, communications had been lost. "Telemetry showed all subsystems working normally before it orbited behind Mars," NASA said in a statement. The spacecraft and operations teams investigated the anomaly, but were unable to restore contact or recover the mission.

MAVEN arrived at Mars in 2014 and began studying the upper Martian atmosphere and its interaction with solar wind. The mission provided critical insights into how Mars lost most of its atmosphere over billions of years. Scientists determined that solar wind and radiation stripped away the planet's upper atmosphere, transforming Mars from a potentially warm, wet world capable of supporting liquid water into the cold, dry desert it is today.

Throughout its operational period, MAVEN made numerous discoveries about atmospheric escape processes and how solar wind interacts with Mars' magnetic field remnants. The spacecraft had far exceeded its original mission timeline, operating successfully for years beyond its planned lifespan.

Beyond its primary atmospheric research, MAVEN served as a communication relay for NASA's two Mars rovers, Curiosity and Perseverance. The loss of this relay capability removes an important tool for maintaining contact with the rovers on the Martian surface.

NASA maintains two other active spacecraft in Mars orbit. The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, launched in 2005, and Mars Odyssey, launched in 2001, continue to operate and study the planet. These missions will help fill some of the gap left by MAVEN's loss, though the spacecraft provided unique data about the upper atmosphere that will be difficult to replace.

The extensive data MAVEN collected during its operational lifetime will continue to inform scientific understanding of planetary atmospheres and climate evolution on Mars for years to come. Researchers plan to analyze the wealth of information gathered by the spacecraft to develop more complete models of how Mars' atmosphere changed over geological time.

MAVEN's conclusion marks the end of one of NASA's longer-running Mars orbital missions. The spacecraft's success in achieving and surpassing its scientific objectives demonstrated the importance of dedicated atmospheric research platforms in planetary science. The mission joins a growing list of retired Mars explorers that have collectively expanded humanity's knowledge of Earth's planetary neighbor.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm detected in South Texas in first US border breach
cards.teaser: The USDA confirmed a case of screwworm infection in South Texas, marking the parasite's first crossing of the US-Mexico border.
cards.body:
The United States Department of Agriculture has confirmed a case of flesh-eating screwworm infection in South Texas. The confirmation represents the first time the parasite has breached the US-Mexico border, according to USDA officials.

Screwworm flies lay eggs in open wounds of warm-blooded animals, and the hatched larvae burrow into living tissue to feed. The parasite was eradicated from the United States decades ago through sustained control programs. The appearance of screwworm in South Texas raises concerns about potential spread and the need for renewed surveillance and control measures in border regions.

cards.headline: Google launches AI Edge Gallery for Mac, enabling local Gemini model operation
cards.teaser: Google released AI Edge Gallery for macOS, allowing Mac users to run Gemini artificial intelligence models directly on their computers without cloud connectivity.
cards.body:
Google has released AI Edge Gallery for macOS, allowing users to run Gemini models directly on their machines without relying on cloud servers. The application brings artificial intelligence processing to local devices, eliminating the need for constant internet connectivity.

The launch features Gemma 4 12B, a multimodal model that processes audio and video content. Google designed it to work on standard laptops with 16GB of RAM, enabling local AI workflows without requiring powerful server infrastructure or cloud dependence.

cards.headline: Geomagnetic storm watch issued for Thursday and Friday
cards.teaser: Federal forecasters issued a G3 geomagnetic storm watch for Thursday and Friday, with northern lights potentially visible in eight states.
cards.body:
Space weather forecasters have issued a G3 geomagnetic storm watch for Thursday and Friday nights, bringing the possibility of aurora borealis displays to parts of the northern United States. Eight states may see the northern lights during the storm period, according to forecasts.

The Pacific Northwest has particular viewing opportunities on Thursday and Friday nights. SpaceWeather.gov updated its watch for the June 4-5 UTC period. G3-level storms represent moderate geomagnetic activity that can produce visible auroras at lower latitudes than typical and may cause minor disruptions to some satellite operations and power grid systems.

cards.headline: Benchmark raises $2 billion in growth fund, breaking decades-long tradition
cards.teaser: Venture capital firm Benchmark departed from its 20-year practice of limiting funds to $425 million by raising its first growth fund as part of a $2 billion capital raise.
cards.body:
Benchmark has raised $2 billion in new capital that includes its first-ever growth fund, marking a significant departure from its long-standing strategy. For more than 20 years, the venture capital firm had maintained a disciplined approach by keeping its funds at approximately $425 million in size.

The growth fund represents a strategic evolution for the Silicon Valley firm. Growth funds typically invest in later-stage companies with demonstrated market traction, allowing Benchmark to participate in larger funding rounds and maintain stakes in maturing portfolio companies.

cards.headline: Apple plans to use Nvidia chips for Gemini-powered Siri upgrade
cards.teaser: Apple intends to deploy Nvidia chips to run a new version of Siri powered by Google's Gemini technology, according to a new report.
cards.body:
Apple plans to launch an upgraded Siri assistant in September that will rely on Nvidia chips and Google's Gemini artificial intelligence technology, according to a report from The Information. The new Siri represents a significant technical shift for Apple's voice assistant.

The timing aligns with Apple's annual fall product launches and comes ahead of the company's Worldwide Developers Conference scheduled for June 8. Industry observers view the conference as a critical moment for Apple to demonstrate its artificial intelligence strategy. The company faces pressure to show competitive AI capabilities as rivals have rapidly deployed generative AI features across consumer products.

cards.headline: Conservation trust reports birth of rare lemur quadruplets
cards.teaser: A wildlife trust announced the birth of lemur quadruplets, a rare occurrence that happens in fewer than 6% of births worldwide.

hero.headline: Knicks take Game 1 of NBA Finals with comeback win over Spurs
hero.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-95 in the opening game of the NBA Finals, extending their remarkable playoff run with a victory on the road. Jalen Brunson led the charge with 30 points as New York erased a significant deficit to claim Game 1 at the Spurs' home court.

The Knicks arrived in San Antonio riding an 11-game winning streak, but faced a Spurs team that had just eliminated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder. Despite the Spurs being led by Victor Wembanyama, the young superstar was kept quiet for long stretches as the Knicks controlled much of the game. The victory puts New York just three wins away from their first championship since 1973.

The Knicks' comeback demonstrated the offensive firepower that has carried them through the playoffs. Brunson took over down the stretch to secure the crucial road win, which gives New York a 1-0 series advantage heading into Game 2.

The series will continue in San Antonio before shifting to New York. The Spurs face immediate pressure to respond at home after failing to protect what had been a strong position earlier in the game. San Antonio must find solutions for the Knicks' late-game execution and Brunson's scoring ability in the coming matchup.

The Spurs reached the Finals by defeating the Thunder in the Western Conference Finals. Victor Wembanyama led the effort with 22 points and seven rebounds in that Game 7 clincher, with Julian Champagnie adding 20 points. The series MVP was emotional after securing the Finals berth, recognizing that a childhood dream was coming true.

"Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," Wembanyama said after defeating Oklahoma City. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

For the Thunder, it marked the end of their championship reign. Despite Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, scoring 35 points with nine assists, Oklahoma City could not overcome the Spurs' balanced attack. Thunder coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the tough loss but remained confident.

"You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he said. "And it's the NBA, there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

The matchup carries historical significance. The last time the Knicks reached the Finals in 1999, they faced the Spurs, who won that series 4-1. Now the franchises meet again with the Knicks seeking their first title in over 50 years and the Spurs attempting to capitalize on their young star's emergence as the league's brightest talent.

cards.headline: Russell Wilson retires from NFL after 14 seasons
cards.teaser: The veteran quarterback announced his retirement and will join CBS in a broadcasting role.
cards.body:
Russell Wilson confirmed his retirement from professional football after 14 seasons in the NFL. The quarterback will transition to a television role at CBS.

Wilson's legacy has become a subject of debate following his final four years in the league. Aaron Glenn commented on Wilson's move to broadcasting, noting his team is evaluating quarterback options moving forward.

cards.headline: Yankees await diagnosis on Aaron Judge rib injury
cards.teaser: The star right fielder will undergo additional tests for a bone bruise near his shoulder.
cards.body:
Aaron Judge will receive further medical evaluation for a rib cage injury described as a bone bruise near his shoulder. The Yankees have announced they are seeking clarity on the condition before determining his availability.

The injury has been characterized as a nagging issue. Judge's status looms over the Yankees as they await a clearer diagnosis from additional testing.

cards.headline: Steelers sign tight end Darnell Washington to four-year extension
cards.teaser: Pittsburgh extended Washington's contract ahead of the 2026 season.
cards.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and tight end Darnell Washington agreed to a four-year extension worth $42 million. Multiple sources confirmed the deal, which some reports described as a five-year arrangement.

The extension represents another significant signing for Pittsburgh ahead of the upcoming season. Washington's new contract secures him as part of the Steelers' offensive plans through the end of the decade.

cards.headline: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver discusses expansion plans
cards.teaser: Silver said conversations about adding new franchises are ongoing.
cards.body:
NBA Commissioner Adam Silver addressed expansion during a media availability before the Finals. He said the league is interested in multiple ownership groups in Las Vegas and Seattle, and that discussions about adding teams continue.

Silver spoke on several topics including tanking and other league matters. The commissioner indicated the NBA is actively considering expansion possibilities in both Western cities.

cards.headline: Russian and Ukrainian players to meet in French Open semifinals
cards.teaser: The ongoing war between the countries will form a backdrop to the women's matches.
cards.body:
Russia's war in Ukraine will cast a shadow over the French Open women's semifinals and potentially the final. The tournament has created an unavoidable backdrop for these matches between players from both nations.

The meetings represent a rare moment for Russian and Ukrainian athletes to compete on an international stage during the ongoing conflict. Tennis authorities have faced significant challenges in determining how to manage participation from both countries throughout the war.

cards.headline: Spain's Lamine Yamal downplays Messi comparisons ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: The 18-year-old forward is a key member of Spain's squad but wants to forge his own path.
cards.body:
At just 18 years old, Lamine Yamal has become a key player in Spain's World Cup squad. The young talent has consistently dismissed comparisons to Lionel Messi, preferring to carve out his own path in international football.

Rather than dwelling on such comparisons, Yamal is focused on establishing his individual identity as a player. His rapid rise in the sport has brought significant attention, but he remains determined to be recognized for his own abilities and contributions to the Spanish team.

hero.headline: Pace Gallery Cuts 50 Artists and 50 Staff Members
hero.body:
Pace Gallery, one of the art world's largest commercial galleries, has reduced its roster by 50 artists and eliminated 50 staff positions. The cuts represent a significant contraction for the mega gallery, which operates locations across multiple cities globally.

The reductions affect both the gallery's artist representation and its workforce. Pace has built a reputation as one of the most prominent contemporary art galleries, representing major artists and maintaining exhibition spaces in cultural capitals around the world. The simultaneous reduction in both artists and staff suggests a restructuring of the gallery's operations and business model.

The art market has faced headwinds in recent years, with economic uncertainty affecting sales and collector spending patterns. Major galleries have grappled with rising operational costs, including rent for prime exhibition spaces and staffing expenses, while navigating shifts in how art is bought and sold. The pandemic accelerated changes in the industry, including increased reliance on online sales and virtual exhibitions.

Pace's decision to shrink reflects broader pressures facing large commercial galleries as they balance expansion ambitions with financial realities. The gallery sector has seen consolidation and closures among mid-sized operations, while major players reassess their footprints. For the 50 artists no longer represented by Pace, the change means finding new gallery representation or alternative ways to show and sell their work.

The staff reductions come at a time when employment in the arts sector remains sensitive to economic conditions. Gallery positions range from curators and sales directors to installers and administrative staff. The cuts will reshape Pace's operations as it moves forward with a smaller team and a more focused artist roster.

These developments at Pace echo challenges across the broader cultural institutions sector. Museums and galleries worldwide are confronting rising operational costs, weak visitor attendance, and pressure on budgets. Many institutions have yet to recover visitor numbers from before the pandemic, while facing new expenses including inflation and increased business rates.

The financial strain on cultural venues reflects wider economic pressures on both institutions and commercial galleries. Competition for people's time and spending has intensified as the cost of living crisis affects discretionary spending on art and culture. Some institutions have implemented voluntary exit schemes and explored compulsory redundancies as they seek to balance their missions with financial sustainability.

Larger galleries and museums are attempting strategic resets to adapt to changed circumstances. These shifts involve difficult decisions about staffing levels, exhibition programming, and operational scope. The challenge for institutions like Pace is positioning themselves for long-term viability while maintaining their role in supporting artists and serving audiences.

The gallery's restructuring underscores how economic headwinds and shifting market conditions force even established players to fundamentally reassess their business models and commitments to artists.

cards.headline: Questlove Directs Earth, Wind & Fire Documentary at Tribeca Festival
cards.teaser: The filmmaker premiered his portrait of the band at the festival's opening night.
cards.body:
Questlove's documentary about Earth, Wind & Fire opened the Tribeca Festival on Wednesday. The film, titled "To Be Celestial vs That's the Weight of the World," tells the band's story and that of founder Maurice White through Questlove's distinctive directorial vision.

The documentary presents a portrait of the legendary but underrated band, capturing their rightful place in popular music history. Questlove's approach balances the group's musical achievements with a deeper exploration of their career, creating a narrative that is both thrilling and haunting.

cards.headline: Robert De Niro Criticizes Trump at Tribeca Festival Opening
cards.teaser: The actor used his opening night remarks to describe the former president as immoral, cruel and corrupt.
cards.body:
Robert De Niro spoke at the Tribeca Festival opening night and directed criticism at Donald Trump. The Oscar winner described Trump as immoral, cruel and corrupt during his time at the podium.

De Niro used the occasion to discuss Tribeca's mission as a festival created after the September 11 attacks. The festival was formed to highlight a part of New York City affected by the attacks.

cards.headline: Doja Cat Insults Elon Musk While Requesting X Platform Change
cards.teaser: The singer called the tech owner a barrel chested Ewok while asking for the return of audio posts.
cards.body:
Doja Cat posted on X requesting that Elon Musk reinstate the platform's audio post feature. In the same message, she insulted Musk, calling him a frog build looking bitch and saying he looks like he eats sand.

The Grammy winner addressed Musk directly in her post. She used several insults, including describing him as having a barrel chest and comparing him to an Ewok.

cards.headline: Josephine Acquires Distribution Rights for Indian Subcontinent
cards.teaser: Fragrant Nature Film Creations secured rights to the Sundance winner starring Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan.
cards.body:
Fragrant Nature Film Creations acquired exclusive distribution rights to "Josephine" across the Indian subcontinent. The deal covers India, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Bangladesh and the Maldives.

The film is directed by Beth de Arajo and stars Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan, who also serve as producers. "Josephine" follows an eight-year-old girl and won at the Sundance Film Festival.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Contestant Apologizes for Using Racial Slur
cards.teaser: Vasana Montgomery was expelled from the show after videos surfaced showing her using the n-word.
cards.body:
Vasana Montgomery, a 25-year-old from Beaverton, Oregon, was expelled from Love Island USA Season 8 after social media videos emerged showing her using racial slurs. She issued a public apology on Wednesday addressing the controversy.

In her Instagram statement, Montgomery acknowledged the videos and stated there is no excuse for the language used. She indicated the videos dated back to her teenage years.

cards.headline: Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury Welcome Second Child
cards.teaser: The reality TV star announced the birth on Instagram with a family photo.
cards.body:
Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury have announced the arrival of their second child. The reality TV star shared the news on Instagram alongside a photograph featuring herself, Fury, their daughter Bambi and their newborn.

The couple, both known for their reality television careers, are now parents to two children.

hero.headline: Trump to nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
hero.body:
President Trump announced at a White House dinner that he plans to nominate Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general, according to a video of the event posted on social media by a White House aide.

Blanche has previously represented Trump in multiple legal matters and currently serves as deputy attorney general. If confirmed by the Senate, he would lead the Department of Justice and serve as the chief law enforcement officer of the federal government. The attorney general position ranks among the most powerful roles in the executive branch, with authority over federal prosecutions, civil rights enforcement, and antitrust matters. The Justice Department also oversees agencies including the FBI and the Bureau of Prisons.

The nomination requires Senate confirmation. The Senate Judiciary Committee will hold hearings to review Blanche's qualifications and record before the full Senate votes on his confirmation. Trump has not yet submitted the formal nomination paperwork to the Senate, but once submitted, the confirmation process will begin with committee review.

Blanche's potential confirmation comes amid controversy over his handling of documents related to Jeffrey Epstein. A lawsuit filed Monday by Katie Phang, an investigative journalist and legal analyst, alleges that Blanche engaged in a "brazen, shocking, and ongoing violation" of a law requiring the Department of Justice to release all documents related to the late sex offender.

Congress passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act in November with a December 19, 2025 deadline for releasing all documents. Phang's lawsuit claims that Blanche has missed statutory deadlines for document production, made improper or excessive redactions, failed to explain redactions as required by law, and withheld or retracted key documents after release. Blanche has argued that redactions were necessary to prevent the inadvertent identification of Epstein's victims, many of whom are minors, though he has acknowledged that "mistakes are inevitable."

Democratic lawmakers have criticized the process. Jamie Raskin, the Democratic ranking member of the House judiciary committee, told reporters in February that there were "tons of completely unnecessary redactions, in addition to the failure to redact the names of victims."

Phang wants the court to declare the Department of Justice in violation of the law and order the release of all required documents without unlawful redactions. The lawsuit also seeks the appointment of an independent special master from outside the department to oversee the agency's compliance with the transparency law.

The Justice Department's office of the inspector general announced last week that it was launching its own audit into the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act, with a preliminary objective of evaluating the agency's processes for identifying, redacting, and releasing records.

cards.headline: Democrats demand answers on White House role in Trump Jr. loan
cards.teaser: Democratic lawmakers are seeking an explanation after reports that a White House official intervened to approve a $620 million Pentagon loan to a company linked to Donald Trump Jr.
cards.body:
Several Democratic lawmakers are demanding answers after a report that a White House official intervened to approve a $620 million Pentagon loan to a company linked to Donald Trump Jr. The lawmakers have called the reported intervention an example of Trump administration corruption.

In their letter, the Democrats are pressing for a full explanation of the process that led to the Pentagon loan being granted to the company associated with Trump's eldest son.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to ceasefire contingent on Hezbollah withdrawal
cards.teaser: Israel and Lebanon reached an agreement for a full ceasefire, conditioned on Hezbollah halting attacks and withdrawing operatives from southern Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israel and Lebanon have agreed to implement a full ceasefire to end hostilities, according to a joint statement from the US State Department. The agreement requires Hezbollah to completely cease fire and withdraw all its fighters from the area south of the Litani River in south Lebanon.

The US emphasized that both countries reject "any attempt, by any state or non-state actor, to hold Lebanon's future hostage." The ceasefire represents a significant development in the Trump administration's broader diplomatic efforts in the Middle East, removing one of the largest barriers to reaching a wider agreement with Iran.

cards.headline: House rebukes Max Miller for remarks about Rashida Tlaib
cards.teaser: The House struck Rep. Max Miller's comments from the record after he accused Rep. Rashida Tlaib of associating with Hezbollah during debate.
cards.body:
The Ohio Republican's remarks were stricken from the record after he made comments about Rep. Rashida Tlaib during debate on a Lebanon war powers resolution. Miller said of Tlaib that Hezbollah is a terrorist organization and its members are butchers that you like to hang out with to a certain extent.

The incident occurred as tensions in the House boiled over during debate on Tlaib's push to pass a Lebanon war powers resolution. The fight had already been dividing Democrats before sparking the cross-partisan exchange that briefly ground the chamber to a halt.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor and could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Haaland won the New Mexico Democratic primary for governor. If elected in the general election, she could make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.

Haaland previously served as an official in the Biden administration. She will face the Republican nominee in the general election for the governorship of New Mexico.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in California's gubernatorial primary as results continue to come in.
cards.body:
Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra are leading in California's gubernatorial primary. Under the state's top-two primary system, all candidates compete on a single ballot, with the highest two vote-getters advancing to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

The race will determine who replaces Gov. Gavin Newsom. Since California is solidly Democratic, the next governor will almost certainly be a Democrat. The primary has highlighted contrasting visions within the party, with establishment-backed Becerra representing a more traditional, corporate-friendly approach, while progressive voices like Tom Steyer offer an alternative direction for the state.

cards.headline: Army identifies soldier killed in Iraq training accident
cards.teaser: The Army identified Sgt. Devin A. Seibel as the American soldier who died along with a British Army soldier during a military training accident in Iraq.
cards.body:
Sgt. Devin A. Seibel, 26, of Robinson, Texas, died on May 31 at Erbil Airbase in what the Pentagon called a training-related incident. The Army released the identification in a statement late Wednesday.

A British Army soldier also died in the training accident. The Pentagon described the incident as training-related at the Iraqi airbase.
